note: A56 T2 stage 1: pricing of the 4D s-parametric verifier on three representatives (window [191/50, 969271/250000], sscale 8, jobs 3).

cost_model.reading: neither the LP margin nor the atom count predicts the 4D cost; the driver is how many s-subdivisions the certificate demands, i.e. how close its tightest covering atom sits to the boundary of Q. Depth, not time, is the binding resource: a run that FAILs at depth 48 typically FAILs fast, and +8 depth costs about 2.5x (k5_15: 277s FAIL at 48 -> 687s PASS at 56).

depth_scaling.note: added by the depth-60/64 completion pass (2026-09-01). Attempts and outcomes:
depth_scaling.correction: The +8-depth ~2.5x factor fitted on k5_15 generalises ONLY to runs that CONVERGE. The depth-48 FAIL times are NOT a cost baseline: they are --max-witnesses aborts (20 witnesses reached and the search stops), so a 0.7 s depth-48 FAIL says nothing about the cost of the completed search. Lifting the depth removes the early witnesses, and the same certificate then explores unboundedly. Observed: 5/5 lifted-depth attempts on the OPEN set timed out at 600-900 s having produced fewer than 20 witnesses.
depth_scaling.operating_point: depth 48 is the affordable regime and is what produced all 21 TRANSFERRED rows. depth 56 pays for a certificate whose tangency is just past the depth-48 horizon (k5_15, k6_23). depth 60 with a <=15 min cap is unaffordable: it converts fast informative FAILs into uninformative TIMEOUTs.

corrected_cost_law.headline: t_4D ~= 261 us x (number of s-splits), Spearman 0.978 on the 21 PASSes. The s-subdivision count is the cost; neither the LP margin (rho -0.35) nor the atom count (rho +0.45) predicts it.
corrected_cost_law.artifact_1_witness_capped_FAIL_times: A FAIL time is NOT a cost measurement. verify_param stops a root box after --max-witnesses-per-box (8) witnesses, so a FAIL reports whatever the DFS reached first and exits. k6_32 'FAILs in 0.7 s' at depth 48 and then runs >900 s at depth 56 and >600 s at depth 60 without finishing. Only PASS times are true costs.
corrected_cost_law.artifact_2_witness_s_ranges_do_not_local: For the same reason the recorded witness_s_range is a sample, not the failing set. A witness s-range localises the failure ONLY when the search completed, i.e. when the witness count is NOT a multiple of the per-box cap 8. Across the whole campaign exactly one run satisfied this: k6_23's full-window run (9 witnesses), and it is exactly the one whose sub-window bisection PASSed. Every other OPEN row reports 16 or 24 witnesses (truncated), and 6 of 7 attempted sub-window bisections FAILed.
corrected_cost_law.depth_scaling_0_of_5: Lifting the depth converted 0 of 5 attempts: k6_32, k5_19 (depth 56 AND 60), k5_20 (60), all timing out at 600-900 s. The +8-depth ~2.5x factor holds only for a run that CONVERGES (k5_15: 277 s FAIL@48 -> 687 s PASS@56). Depth 48 is the affordable regime and produced all 21 original TRANSFERRED rows; depth 56 pays only for a certificate whose tangency sits just past the depth-48 horizon.

sub_window_bisection.what: verify_param on the complementary sub-window of the recorded witness band
sub_window_bisection.verdict: WORKS ONLY WHEN THE WITNESS SET IS COMPLETE (see artifact 2)
sub_window_bisection.results: 2 successes / 8 windows attempted: k6_23 [191/50, 3877/1000] (2888 s, 99.85% of the window) and k6_07 [191/50, 956767/250000] (173 s, 12.4%). k6_28, k5_14, k5_20, k6_32, k5_04, k6_19 all FAILed on their complementary windows (0.5-144 s each).
sub_window_bisection.price: one depth-48 run per window, 0.5-2900 s; cheap to attempt, low hit rate

resolve_with_margin.what: re-solve the guard LP with a ROW-SHRINK robustness margin eps_geo, so every covering atom must sit at least eps_geo INSIDE Q, then re-certify at the largest weight scale the budget allows and re-run the 4D verifier
resolve_with_margin.verdict: CONVERTS. 3 of 4 sampled certificates went from OPEN to full-window PASS.
resolve_with_margin.the_lever_is_eps_geo_not_the_weight_scal: k6_08 was first re-solved with witness-feedback rows and scale 1.03 -> 1.06 and STILL failed the 4D run (26 s). The same certificate with eps_geo = 0.003 converted in 12 s total. Scaling weights cannot help when coverage at the weak placement rests on ONE atom that must lie inside Q: the mass is already >= 1, it is the atom's POSITION that has no slack. eps_geo buys exactly that slack, and it is the same quantity the 4D verifier needs against the atom's s-interval.
resolve_with_margin.witness_feedback_was_inert: In all four sampled runs the witness glob matched 0 files (the sweep writes <name>.param.wit.json, the glob looked for *.witnesses.json), so n_4d_witnesses = 0 and the three conversions are due to eps_geo ALONE. The glob is fixed in resolve_margin.py, but the priced result stands without witness feedback.

prices.k6_08: CONVERTS in 12.0 s (LP 7.6 + certify 0.9 + 4D 1.5); new cert 4 atoms, margin 0.760
prices.k6_28: CONVERTS in 96.7 s (LP 49.5 + certify 2.8 + 4D 39.4); new cert 9 atoms, margin 0.230
prices.k6_32: CONVERTS in 677.3 s (LP 651.9 + certify 2.8 + 4D 17.9); new cert 452 atoms, margin 0.230. The LP dominates; the 4D run is 18 s.
prices.k5_02: INFEASIBLE at eps_geo = 0.003: tau rose to exactly 6.000000 = budget. A certificate with total margin 0.00055 cannot pay for 0.003 of positional slack. Retry with eps_geo ~ 0.0003.

resolve_with_margin.robustness_budget_rule: eps_geo is affordable iff the re-solved tau stays below the budget. The observed cost of eps_geo = 0.003 was tau 4.000 -> 4.500 for k6_28/k6_32 (0.5 of budget) and 0 for k6_08. So certificates with budget - tau >= ~0.5 can afford it; the thin ones need eps_geo scaled down in proportion.
resolve_with_margin.caveat: a converted row kills the STRATUM over the window, but via a NEW base certificate; the original A53/A54 certificate stays s0-only.
resolve_with_margin.recipe_steps: see the module docstring of code/resolve_margin.py (steps 1-5)

final_sweep.eps_threshold_rule: eps_geo >= 0.0015 converted 13 of 16; eps_geo < 0.0015 converted 0 of 5. The row shrink must exceed the positional deficit at the weak placement, and that deficit is of order 1.5e-3 across this library. Since eps_geo is capped by the LP slack budget - tau, a certificate can be repaired iff its slack buys at least ~1.5e-3 of shrink -- empirically budget - tau >= ~0.5.
final_sweep.schedule_used: eps_geo = clamp(0.003 * min(1, (budget - tau_0)/1.0), 0.0002, 0.003), tau_0 from the A53 node json
final_sweep.cost_shape: LP-dominated as predicted: median LP 433 s, median certify 3 s, median 4D 45 s. The 4D verification is now a rounding error; a converted row costs 12-680 s end to end. FAILED rows cost MORE than successes (certify burns its full witness-feedback rounds before giving up): k6_29 1480 s of certify, k6_27 1485 s, k5_02 1497 s.
